pr_title: Use new row primitives for ResizeTraditional
pr_body:
This will allow us to share the same fundamental text insertion
logic for both `ResizeTraditional` and `Reflow`, because both
can be implemented with `ROW::CopyRangeFrom`. It also replaces
the `BufferAllocator` struct with a `_allocateBuffer` function
which will help us allocate scratch buffer rows in the future.

Closes #14696

## PR Checklist
* Disable reflow resize in conhost
* Print "zhwik8.txt" - a enwik8.txt equivalent of Chinese Wikipedia
* Run `color 80` in cmd
* Resize windows from 120 to 119 columns
* Wide glyphs disappear and are replaced with whitespace ✅
* Resizing the window to >120 columns adds gray whitespace ✅

issue_context.title: TextBuffer::ResizeTraditional may leak stale pointers
issue_context.body: The catch clause will allow `BufferAllocator` to be destroyed while the `ROW`s in `_storage` continue to reference its memory. The solution is to refactor `ROW::Resize` from being a mutating function over to allocating a new `_storage` vector and copying all rows over. That way the `TextBuffer` is only mutated once at the end, long after all throwing code has finished executing.

review_comments: begin never changes; sup with it?

In the current version of `CopyRangeFrom` it returns the `columnEnd` of the `dest` row, while the `begin` parameter (also called `otherBegin`) is modified to be the `columnEnd` of the source row. This allows you to implement reflow, by calling `CopyRangeFrom` until either of the two integers has exceeded their corresponding row width.

The API design is terrible and could use a `RowWriteState`-like struct... But I think that's a rather simple change to make and can be done at any point in time.
